guards.what: N1: the two conditions permafrost.py:28 drops from Permafrost.cs:47 -- `CombatManager.Instance.IsInProgress` and `cardPlay.Card.Owner == base.Owner`
guards.rationale: Both are structurally satisfied. on_card_played is a combat hook dispatched only by a live CombatState, and combat.py:493-494 breaks the play loop once the fight is decided, so the IsInProgress test cannot fail at the sim's dispatch site (the residual difference -- that C# refuses the whole dispatch once the combat is ending -- is audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json guard G8's mechanism, labelled DORMANT there, and is not re-derived here per binding rule 3). The card-owner test is multiplayer scoping: the sim has one player and dispatches card hooks only for that player's plays. guards.what: N2: `BlockVar(7m, ValueProp.Unpowered)` (Permafrost.cs:33) read through `base.DynamicVars.Block` at the single call site (Permafrost.cs:50) vs `BLOCK = 7` and `props=ValueProp.UNPOWERED` (permafrost.py:21, 31)
guards.rationale: No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in the file, so 7 is the pinned non-ascension value, and the port carries the Unpowered flag explicitly rather than letting BlockCmd infer it -- which matters because cmds.py:145 gates the block additive/multiplicative stage on the same is_powered_attack rule as damage, so an Unpowered block is deliberately not scaled by Dexterity-adjacent modifiers on either side. Checked per PROMPT.md bug class 19 (a constant protected by a citation that looks verified): the docstring's '7 Block' and the C# BlockVar agree. NOTE per binding rule 7: cmds.py is not hashed here.

guards.what: N3: C# sets `ActivatedThisCombat = true` AFTER awaiting CreatureCmd.GainBlock (Permafrost.cs:50-51); the sim sets `_activated = True` BEFORE calling BlockCmd.apply (permafrost.py:29-31)
guards.rationale: The orders differ but no reachable path distinguishes them: nothing between the two statements can play another Power card. BlockCmd.apply dispatches only the block modifier and block-gained hooks, none of which plays a card, and C#'s CreatureCmd.GainBlock is likewise not a card-play path. The sim's order is additionally re-entrancy-safe, so if a future ported effect ever did play a card from a block-gained hook the sim would grant the block once and the game would grant it twice -- recorded so that a later reader does not mistake the reordering for a defect, and so the direction of the residual risk is on record. Same observable outcome today, so faithful rather than deliberate-divergence.
